title: Lior and the Autopsy
premise: Felix Iversen, the meticulous coroner of the fading town of Marrow's Bend, is hired by a nervous stranger named Ada Quill to prove that a murder scheduled for the spring equinox will never happen — a prediction she claims comes from her brother, Lior, who everyone in town buried three years ago. As Felix digs into the town's founding families, they discover Lior's coffin was empty and that he witnessed a fatal cover-up involving the beloved Harrow family, whose heir stands trial for a death no one believes was murder. The 'future murder' is actually a threat: someone intends to kill Lior before he can testify. Felix must find Lior alive, protect him from both the Harrows' enforcers and their own growing doubts about Ada's honesty, and choose between loyalty to the town that raised them and the truth rotting beneath its graves. In the end, Lior testifies, the trial cracks open the cover-up, and Felix — having lost their reputation but gained an unlikely found family with Ada and Lior — reopens every cold case the Harrows touched.
about_author: Sable Reyes spent a decade as a rural records clerk before turning to fiction, a job that taught them how much truth hides in filing errors. They write mysteries about small towns where everyone remembers everything except what matters.

chapters.title: The Man Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Felix Iversen's POV. A stranger, Ada Quill, arrives at the coroner's office with a retainer: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. She won't say whose or how she knows. Felix, proud of closing every case, takes the money against their better judgment. Beat: uneasy curiosity.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Felix walks the cemetery cataloguing plots, establishing their intimate knowledge of Marrow's Bend and its dead. They find Lior Quill's headstone, dated three years back, and remember the closed-casket funeral. Beat: quiet pride shadowed by a first thread of doubt.

chapters.title: Closed Casket
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Felix's POV to Lior's funeral: the Harrow family paid for it, the body was never viewed, and young Felix signed off on paperwork they didn't fully read. Beat: guilt surfacing like a bruise.

chapters.title: The Prediction
chapters.summary: Ada explains: her brother wrote letters from hiding predicting his own murder on the spring equinox, six weeks away. She shows Felix one letter, postmarked locally. Someone in town knows Lior lives. Beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: Trial Docket
chapters.summary: Felix pulls court records: Cassian Harrow, golden-boy heir, stands trial for the hit-and-run death of dockworker Tomas Reyes — unless the case collapses for lack of a witness. The witness on record is listed as deceased: Lior Quill. Beat: the pieces begin to align.

chapters.title: The Harrow Table
chapters.summary: Third-person limited through matriarch Odile Harrow. She hosts a family dinner where Cassian's anxiety frays the performance of innocence; she quietly instructs the family lawyer to 'handle the witness problem.' Beat: menace behind civility.

chapters.title: Exhumation Request
chapters.summary: Felix files to exhume Lior's grave, citing irregularities. The town council — half Harrow employees — stalls it. Felix feels the machinery of the town turn against them for the first time. Beat: isolation.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks Felix's office, stealing the retainer file but leaving the cash. Ada appears afterward, too quickly, knowing too much about what was taken. Felix begins suspecting her of playing both sides. Beat: suspicion.

chapters.title: The Dockworker's Daughter
chapters.summary: Felix visits Tomas Reyes's daughter, Nell, who insists her father feared the Harrows and kept a ledger of their shipping fraud. She gives Felix a torn page. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Ledger Lines
chapters.summary: The ledger page shows payments routed through the coroner's office — meaning someone inside falsified Lior's death certificate. Felix realizes their own predecessor may have been complicit. Beat: betrayal close to home.

chapters.title: Old Mentors
chapters.summary: Felix confronts retired coroner Ambrose Pell, who signed the death record. Ambrose, dying and frightened, admits he never saw a body — only instructions and money — and warns Felix to stop digging. Beat: pity and anger entwined.

chapters.title: Equinox Countdown
chapters.summary: Structural midpoint pivot: Felix maps the timeline — four weeks to the equinox, two weeks to trial. They commit fully to finding Lior alive, hiring Nell as an unlikely ally. Beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
chapters.summary: A tip leads to a decommissioned lighthouse north of town. Felix finds signs of recent habitation: canned food, a stack of unsent letters addressed to Ada. Lior was here — days ago. Beat: hope sharpened by urgency.

chapters.title: Letters to My Sister
chapters.summary: Reading Lior's letters, Felix learns his story: he saw Cassian's car strike Tomas and was smuggled out of town by someone inside the Harrow house. The letters name only 'the friend.' Beat: intimacy with a man he's never met.

chapters.title: Inside the House
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We learn the 'friend' was Odile herself — a flicker of conscience now turned liability. She orders the lighthouse watched, not burned, wanting Lior found quietly. Beat: a villain's divided heart.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Felix notices surveillance on their own home. With Nell's help, they run a counter-tail on the Harrow fixer, Marek Voss, and photograph him meeting the stalled council members. Beat: small victory, larger fear.

chapters.title: What Ada Knew
chapters.summary: Felix corners Ada: she admits she's been receiving Lior's letters for years and hid it, terrified that revealing him would get him killed faster. Trust fractures, then partially mends over shared coffee at 3 a.m. Beat: wounded honesty.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: The exhumation finally proceeds under public pressure. The coffin holds sandbags and a stranger's shoes. The town square watches; the Harrows cannot un-see it. Beat: public detonation of the secret.

chapters.title: Cassian Cracks
chapters.summary: Cassian Harrow, drunk, nearly confesses to Felix at a bar — then Marek drags him out. Felix realizes Cassian may be guilty of panic and concealment but not the killing itself. Beat: moral complication.

chapters.title: Who Was Driving
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the night of Tomas's death, Felix finds tire and medical evidence pointing to a second vehicle — and a second driver. The trial's premise itself begins to wobble. Beat: the mystery deepens past its obvious answer.

chapters.title: Nell's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nell decodes more of her father's ledger: Tomas wasn't killed for witnessing the fraud — he was blackmailing whoever drove. His death was a negotiation gone wrong. Beat: the victim grows complicated.

chapters.title: Marek's Price
chapters.summary: Felix offers Marek immunity-adjacent leverage: photos of his council bribes. Marek reveals only that Lior is 'somewhere he chose to be,' and that Odile isn't the one who wants him dead. Beat: the threat relocates.

chapters.title: The Other Letter
chapters.summary: Felix discovers a letter in the office files — planted during the break-in — warning them off in handwriting matching Ambrose Pell's. But Ambrose died last week. Someone is forging a dead man. Beat: chill.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Box
chapters.summary: Searching Ambrose's effects, Felix finds originals of Lior's death certificate plus a second name erased from the file: Juniper Harrow, Cassian's sister, who left town after the accident. Beat: a new suspect surfaces.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: Tracking Juniper to a coastal town two counties away, Felix and Ada find her living under another name. She confirms she was driving that night — with Cassian asleep beside her — and that Lior saw her face. Beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: Why He Ran
chapters.summary: Juniper explains Lior didn't flee the Harrows; he fled her. She begged him to stay silent, and when he refused, she helped him disappear rather than let Marek silence him permanently. Beat: tangle of guilt and mercy.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: One day remains. Ada receives a final letter from Lior naming a meeting place: the cemetery, at his own grave, at dawn. It reads like a trap. Everyone knows. Beat: coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: Dawn at the Grave
chapters.summary: Felix stakes out the cemetery. Instead of Lior, Marek arrives — then turns his gun on Felix, revealing he was hired not by Odile but by the councilmen burying the bribery evidence. Beat: betrayal of expectation.

chapters.title: Lior Rises
chapters.summary: Lior emerges from the crypt tunnels he's used for years — he never left Marrow's Bend at all. He tackles Marek; Nell and Ada subdue him until the sheriff, finally choosing a side, makes the arrest. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Witness Testifies
chapters.summary: Courtroom chapter. Lior, gaunt and steady, describes the night Tomas died; Juniper surrenders herself mid-testimony. Cassian's alibi collapses and reforms around the truth: he covered for his sister. Beat: truth costing everyone something.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Juniper pleads to manslaughter; Cassian to obstruction. Odile, publicly ruined, pays restitution without apology — but privately tells Felix she was the friend in the letters, and asks if mercy was a mistake. Felix doesn't answer. Beat: ambiguous grace.

chapters.title: What the Town Buried
chapters.summary: Fallout: the council resigns, the exhumation report goes public, and Felix's old cases are flagged for review. Some colleagues shun them; others quietly deliver boxes of ignored files. Beat: cost and vindication together.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Funeral
chapters.summary: Felix buries their mentor properly, this time reading every line of the service. They forgive him halfway and decide to live with the other half. Beat: mourning without resolution.

chapters.title: Three Chairs
chapters.summary: Quiet domestic chapter: Ada and Lior, technically dead and legally reborn, move into the apartment above Felix's office. Found-family rhythms form — bad cooking, shared case files, Lior learning to walk in daylight again. Beat: warmth earned.

chapters.title: The Reopened Files
chapters.summary: Felix and Nell begin reviewing the cold cases the Harrow money touched. One file — a drowning from twelve years ago — makes Felix go still. Beat: hook of unfinished business.

chapters.title: Confession at the Counter
chapters.summary: Cassian, pre-sentencing, meets Felix at a diner and admits he knew about the drowning too — that the Harrow rot runs deeper than one accident. He asks Felix to look at it 'for the town, not for me.' Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: The equinox passes, the predicted date of murder come and gone. Ada burns the last of the warning letters; Lior carves a new stone for his own grave reading 'misreported.' Beat: release.

chapters.title: The Drowning File
chapters.summary: Felix opens the twelve-year-old case at their desk, Lior and Ada reading over their shoulders. First clue lands: the victim's autopsy was signed by Ambrose Pell. Beat: determination renewed.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Closing meditation from Felix's POV walking the cemetery at dusk: loyalty to the living now means loyalty to the truth about the dead. They name every grave, including the ones the town got wrong. Beat: peace with vigilance.

chapters.title: Case Open
chapters.summary: Final scene: a new client knocks — a woman claiming her brother drowned, though the file says otherwise. Felix looks at Ada and Lior, then unlocks the door. 'Sit down,' they say. 'Tell me everything.' Beat: the door stays open.
